privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.note: FuturePilot is a project under active development, built by one person. This policy describes exactly what the system does today: it was written by reading the code, not copied from a template. What is still unresolved is stated as such rather than hidden. This text has not been reviewed by a lawyer.
privacy.whoTitle: Who is responsible for your data
privacy.who: FuturePilot is built and run by Luci Jabba, independently. There is no company behind it, no investors, and no partners with access to the database. For anything concerning your data the contact is direct: ljfuturepilot@gmail.com.
privacy.whatIntro: This is the complete list. There are no hidden categories.
privacy.whatAccount: Account: your email, your name if you choose to enter one (it is optional), and your password turned into an irreversible hash. The password itself is never stored and cannot be recovered, not even by whoever administers the server.
privacy.whatTest: Assessment: your answers and the results generated from them — your profile across dimensions, the careers you matched with, and your route.
privacy.whatPassport: Passport: the country and city you pick, the languages you list, your goals, and a profile photo if you choose to upload one. The photo is the most sensitive piece of data in the whole application, and uploading it is always optional: the passport works the same without it.
privacy.whatActivity: Activity: the stamps you earn, the milestones you mark as done, and when that happened. This exists so that when you come back you find your progress where you left it.
privacy.whatTech: Technical: your IP address is used only to limit how many requests one origin can make in a row, and it lives only in the server's memory. It is never written to the database and disappears on restart. We use no tracking cookies and no advertising identifiers.
privacy.why: For one thing only: giving you the guidance you came for, and having it there as you left it when you return. Your answers feed the engine that computes your profile and your route. They are not used to profile you commercially, to train models, or to decide anything about you outside the application.
privacy.share: Nobody. FuturePilot has no analytics, no advertising, no social media buttons, and no embedded third-party services. Fonts are served from our own server instead of requested from Google, precisely so that no third party learns you visited this page. The browser is forbidden, by security policy, from connecting to any domain other than ours.
privacy.shareAI: The engine that analyses your assessment is ours and runs on our server. Your answers are not sent to any external artificial intelligence. This was a deliberate decision: we did not want a school student's answers travelling into another company's infrastructure.
privacy.shareMail: The only information that leaves the server is an email, and only if you ask to reset your password: it goes to your own address through a mail server. That email contains a temporary link, never your password.
privacy.minorsIntro: FuturePilot is made for school students, so we assume a good share of the people using it are minors. That obliges us to more care, not less.
privacy.minorsLaw: In Colombia, processing the data of children and adolescents is governed by Law 1581 of 2012 and Decree 1377 of 2013: it must serve the best interest of the minor, respect their right to be heard, and have the authorisation of whoever holds parental authority.
privacy.minorsPractice: In practice this means that if you are a minor you should create your account with the knowledge of your parent or guardian, and that they may at any time ask to see, correct, or delete your data by writing to the contact address. It also means we ask for the minimum: we do not ask for your ID number, your address, your school, your phone, or your parents' names, because none of that is needed to guide you.
privacy.minorsPending: What is not yet implemented, stated plainly: there is still no technical mechanism that verifies age or collects a guardian's authorisation before an account is created. It is the project's main outstanding privacy task and will be addressed before any general public launch.
privacy.timeSession: The session that keeps you logged in expires after 30 days. Password reset links expire after one hour and stop working the moment you use them.
privacy.timeRest: Everything else — your account, your assessment, your passport, and your progress — is kept for as long as your account is open, because the whole point is that you can come back months later and find your route. It is deleted when you ask. There is not yet an automatic deletion deadline for inactivity; that decision is still pending.
privacy.rightsTitle: What you can do with your data
privacy.rightsIntro: These rights are not a promise in a document: they are built into the application and work today.
privacy.rightsExport: Download everything of yours as a file, from your account. It includes your profile, your results, and your passport.
privacy.rightsDelete: Delete your account, also from your account. Doing so removes your user, your passport, your stamps, your sessions, and your goals. Your assessment result is detached from you: its owner is removed and any name or email carried inside it is wiped, so it remains anonymous usage data that cannot be linked back to you.
privacy.rightsFix: Correct anything that is wrong, by editing your passport or writing to us.
privacy.rightsAsk: Ask what we hold about you and why. You will get an answer.
privacy.sec: Passwords go through PBKDF2-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations and a different salt per user before touching disk. Sessions use a random token of which we store only a fingerprint, so not even reading the database lets someone impersonate you. The browser may only load resources from our own domain, which closes the door on scripts injected from outside. The admin panel requires an account explicitly marked as administrator and keeps a record of what it does.
privacy.secHonest: What we will not overstate: the data lives on a single server in a SQLite database. That is an appropriate architecture for the project's current size, but it does not have the redundancy or the external audits of a large service. If that changes, this page changes with it.
privacy.changes: If what we store or how we use it changes, this page and the date above are updated. If the change is significant, you will be told inside the application.
privacy.contact: Write to ljfuturepilot@gmail.com — for questions, to request your data, to demand we delete it, or if you are a parent or guardian and want to know what we hold about your child.

terms.title: Terms and conditions
terms.note: FuturePilot is free, it helps you explore careers and build a route, and it decides nothing for you. What follows explains that in detail, with no fine print. This text has not been reviewed by a lawyer.
terms.what: A vocational guidance platform. You answer an assessment, an engine computes your profile across dimensions, and from there it shows you careers that fit, universities where you could study them, and a route with concrete steps. It is aimed mainly at school students deciding what to study.
terms.free: It is free. There are no paid plans, no subscriptions, no premium tier, and you will never be asked for a card. If that ever changes, you will be told beforehand, and nothing you already use for free will start costing money.
terms.notTitle: What it is NOT, and this matters
terms.notAdvice: The assessment result is guidance, not a verdict. It is not a psychological diagnosis, it is not signed off by a psychologist or a school counsellor, and it does not replace talking to your counsellor, your teachers, or your family. If a career comes up that does not feel like you, it does not mean you got it wrong: it means a model compared your answers against a set of requirements, nothing more.
terms.notAdmission: It guarantees no university admission, no scholarship, and no job. FuturePilot has no agreement with the institutions listed and plays no part in their selection processes.
terms.notData: University and programme information is curated by hand and can go out of date: requirements, costs, and course offerings change every year. Before making a real decision, always check the institution's official page.
terms.who: Any student. Because the platform is aimed at people in secondary school, we assume many will be minors: if that is you, you should create your account with the knowledge of your parent or guardian. How we handle minors' data is explained in the privacy policy.
terms.accountKeep: Your password is yours; do not share it with anyone. Nobody from FuturePilot will ever ask you for it, by email or by any other means: if someone does, they are not from here.
terms.accountOne: One account per person. Registering with someone else's email, or passing yourself off as another person, is not allowed.
terms.accountLose: If you lose access, there is email recovery. If you lose the email too, there is no way to give the account back: passwords are hashed irreversibly and not even whoever administers the server can read them.
terms.yours: Your answers, your results, your goals, and your passport are yours. We do not publish them, we do not sell them, and we do not use them for anything other than giving you your guidance. You can download or delete them whenever you like from your account.
terms.ours: The code, the design, the writing, and the analysis engine belong to FuturePilot. Use the platform as much as you want, including quoting your results wherever they are useful to you; what you may not do is copy the platform and present it as your own, or resell it.
terms.fairIntro: Little, and all of it reasonable:
terms.fairAbuse: Do not try to take the service down, flood it with automated requests, or get into other people's accounts.
terms.fairHonest: Answer the assessment as you actually are, not as you think looks “better”. The result is only worth anything if the answers are really yours.
terms.fairReport: If you find a security flaw, tell us instead of using it. It is genuinely appreciated and you will get a reply.
terms.up: This is a project under active development maintained by one person. It can go down, it can be in maintenance, and a feature can change or disappear from one day to the next. There is no uptime guarantee and no committed response time.
terms.upBackup: Reasonable care is taken not to lose data, but it cannot be promised that it will never happen. If your results matter to you, download them from your account: the option exists for exactly that.
terms.endYou: You can delete your account whenever you want, yourself, from inside the application. There is nobody to write to and no approval to wait for.
terms.endUs: We may close an account if it is used to attack the service or to impersonate another person. Beyond that, accounts are not closed.
terms.liab: FuturePilot is offered as is, free, and in good faith. Decisions about your education are yours to make, ideally talking them through with your family and your school. We are not answerable for decisions taken solely on what this platform says, nor for third-party information that has gone out of date. What we do take on is our own part: looking after your data as the privacy policy describes, and telling the truth about what the application does.
terms.law: These terms are governed by Colombian law, including Law 1581 of 2012 on personal data protection.
terms.changes: If these terms change, this page and the date above are updated. If the change is significant, you will be told inside the application.
terms.contact: Write to ljfuturepilot@gmail.com. A person replies, not a form.
